title: Step-Down Bridge Guidance Scheduling for Dual-CFG in Video-Audio Diffusion

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to improve speech fidelity in joint video-audio diffusion where constant bridge guidance crowds out text-condition sensitivity in late denoising steps. No prior paper explicitly addresses this specific objective. While several papers discuss guidance scheduling (e.g., [1], [4], [9], [19], [25]), their focus is on improving image fidelity or prompt alignment rather than addressing the specific issue of text-condition sensitivity in joint video-audio diffusion. Papers like [10] and [24] discuss challenges in text-to-sounding video generation and speech-driven animation, but they do not target the specific problem of speech fidelity degradation due to constant bridge guidance.

### Mechanism
The mechanism, "Step-Down bridge guidance scheduling," is a training-free modification for MOVA's dual-CFG that ramps down guidance scale in late denoising steps. Papers [1], [4], [9], [19], and [25] all discuss dynamic or adaptive guidance scheduling in diffusion models. For example, [1] applies guidance in a limited interval, [4] introduces dynamic negative guidance, [9] uses annealing guidance scales, and [19] proposes dynamic CFG scheduling. These mechanisms are substantively equivalent to the contribution's approach of modifying guidance scales dynamically during the denoising process, even though the specific ramping schedule and application domain differ.

### Evaluation
The evaluation uses Verse-Bench speech prompts to measure WER improvement and synchronization quality. Papers like [10] and [24] evaluate text-to-sounding video generation and speech-driven animation, respectively, but do not use Verse-Bench or similar benchmarks. However, the evaluation design — measuring fidelity improvements and synchronization quality — aligns with standard practices in diffusion model validation. Papers such as [1], [4], [9], [19], and [25] use similar evaluation designs (e.g., fidelity metrics, synchronization quality, or prompt alignment) for assessing guidance scheduling. Therefore, the evaluation design is covered.

### Domain
The domain is joint video-audio diffusion generation. Papers [10] and [24] operate in closely related areas, such as text-to-sounding video generation and speech-driven 3D facial animation. These papers address multimodal generation tasks involving video and audio, making the domain substantively equivalent.
